- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecasted decline, actual price often lags and reverses — adjust downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price history shows mean reversion, model often underestimates — increase forecast by 1–3% to align with recent mean.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong price moves — if forecast exceeds 3σ above recent mean, reduce by 10–20% to avoid overshoot.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in high-sentiment periods — add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment >0.6 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model often misjudges trend direction — favor smoother, trend-following adjustments over sharp pivots.
